List has been revised.

2. Heard Ms. Aparna Burman, learned Amicus Curiae and Sri Ashutosh Srivastava, learned A.G.A.
for the State and also perused the record.

3. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 755 of 2018, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 of IPC, Police Station Kotwali Dehat,
District Bulandshahr, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.
4. As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to have impersonated himself by showing himself to be Bhanu Pratap at one stage and Manoj at another and got himself a job in Assam Rifles.

sentences.text: Learned Amicus Curiae has stated that the matter of civil in nature has been converted into a criminal one as the Original Suit No.566 of 2016 has been instituted by the very same informant Bali against the applicant and other family members regarding the property dispute.

Learned Amicus Curiae has also placed reliance on paragraph-6 of the said original suit whereby it has been stated that the applicant was known by both the names i.e. Bhanu Pratap and Manoj, as such, the averments made in the FIR stand falsified.
Learned Amicus Curiae has also stated the after thorough investigation, the police has been pleased to file closure report in the instant case on 01.03.2019.
Subsequent to it, on the protest petition, the matter has been sent for further investigation vide order dated 31.10.2023 by the learned Magistrate concerned.
6. Learned Amicus Curiae has also stated that the applicant is maliciously being prosecuted in the present case due to ulterior motive and has apprehension of his arrest.
He has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged by the prosecution.
Learned Amicus Curiae has further stated that the applicant is the public servant having no criminal history to his credit, is entitled for anticipatory bail.
In case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed, he will not misuse the liberty and shall cooperate with trial.

7. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned Amicus Curiae and also the fact that the applicant has no criminal history.

8. Considering the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations and also taking into consideration the fact that there is a civil suit pending between the parties two years prior to the instant FIR coupled with the fact that closure report has been filed in the instant matter and on protest petition, matter has been sent for further investigation, I find it a fit case to enlarge the applicant on anticipatory bail.
9.
Without expressing any opinion upon ultimate merits of the case either ways which may adversely affect the trial of the case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.

12. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
13. Ms. Aparna Burman, learned Amicus Curiae has assisted the Court very diligently.
This Court provide that she shall be paid counsel's fee as Rs.15,000/-.

Learned Registrar General of this Court is directed to ensure payment of aforesaid fee to Ms. Aparna Burman, learned Amicus Curiae,
without any delay and, in any case, within one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgement/order.
14. Office is directed to provide a copy of this order to the learned Registrar General at the earliest for necessary compliance.
